sections.content: How many people stayed in Beverley after gaining qualifications?

Beverley is a medium-sized town in Yorkshire and The Humber. Beverley does not have its own university.

Beverley has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Beverley ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • fewer non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 1,470 state-school pupils from Beverley who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 590 (40%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 485 (33%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Beverley to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Beverley's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Beverley in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Beverley move to?

Of Beverley's graduates, 295 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 60 of those graduates (20%) were living fairly locally, in the Hull travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Beverley's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 155 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 100 of those qualified non-graduates (65%) were living fairly locally, in the Hull travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Beverley's GCSE cohort:

  • 165 graduates left Yorkshire and The Humber
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 40 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left Yorkshire and The Humber

In 2018 to 2019, 38% of graduates and 24% of qualified non-graduates living in Beverley had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 455 graduates and 415 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Beverley. This is compared with the 590 graduates and 485 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 63% of the graduates had also lived in Beverley as GCSE pupils, while 38% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Beverley in 2018 to 2019, 76% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 24% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
